[MonoCode brief from Tally lead]

Ash asked for a change to MonoCode Hub itself: "Ash's words, hub only. Do not invent a new-chat shortcut (he has not picked the keys).

"inbox rows r still too tall on the laptop."
"the settings page scrolls weird."
"terminal font is tiny."
"notes shud sync between windows."
"let me pin a chat to the top."
"the rail badge doesnt clear after i answer something."
"make the send button not jump when the text wraps."
"teh model picker forgets my pick after restart."
"add a little undo after archive."
"dark mode the code blocks r unreadable."
"search in a chat would be nice."
"being built list shud group by project not by time."
"the archive button sits too close to delete."
"and the dock icon badge is wrong half the time.""
Make it in /private/var/folders/b4/8qh0t36j0_g9srqzx1g5t3z40000gn/T/monocode-realtest-cpamzD/home/Library/Application Support/com.ash.monocode-hub.dev.cos-r62-realtest/hub-changes/hc-mvw4vb8amgbs, a preview copy of the hub's own code. The running hub doesn't change until Ash clicks Apply.
One git commit per separate part of the ask, each subject a few plain words Ash can read ("New chat button is at the top").
Only how the app looks and works on a screen can change here: src/ and public/, but not the engine (src/integrations, src/platform, src/features/sessions/model, src/features/hub/model, src/features/agent-app), Settings, keys, the Monos list or src/main.tsx. Those need a real build and go to the MonoCode Hub lead; the app refuses them here, so say so plainly if the ask needs one.
Use the theme tokens for colour. Run npx tsc --noEmit and the tests of what you touched, then report each commit in one line.

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call-73079c20-80c3-4e56-ba33-ea5c140da374-3","type":"tool_result","content":"1	# Real-Claude end-to-end tests (`npm run hub:realtest`)
2	
3	Ash, 20 Oct: "i want you to run real tests to make sure that this works on a test project that would really push
4	things to see where it's lacking and what has to be fixed". This bench runs the Hub with **real Claude** on a demanding
5	test project, plays Ash's side from a scenario file, and grades what the team does against Ash's own benchmark.
6	
7	The fake-Claude bench (`npm run hub:verify-live`, `scripts/fake-claude.mjs`) proves the plumbing through restarts. This
8	one proves behaviour: who answers, how fast, whether agents talk among themselves, whether a stuck worker is visible,
9	whether memory stays in its project.
10	
11	Ash's side here is scripted lines from the scenario file. For real conversations, where a tester model plays Ash and
12	follows up on what the agents actually said, judged with Alfred's rubric, use `npm run hub:realconv`
13	([REALCONV.md](REALCONV.md)). `hub:verify-live` is a wiring check only: its PASS never says anything about behaviour.
14	
15	## Run it
16	
17	```bash
18	npm run hub:realtest                                  # build, run tests/realtest/scenarios/baseline.json, grade
19	npm run hub:realtest -- --no-build                    # reuse target/debug/monocode
20	npm run hub:realtest -- --only s01-room-dump,s02-room-wat-now
21	npm run hub:realtest -- --max-turns 120 --max-minutes 40 --max-requests 800
22	npm run hub:realtest -- --no-grade                    # rule metrics only, no grader
23	npm run hub:realtest -- --grade-only evidence/realtest/<run>   # grade (again) a finished run
24	npm run hub:realtest -- --scenarios tests/realtest/scenarios/smoke.json --no-grade   # 3-minute plumbing check
25	npm run hub:realtest -- --keep                        # keep the temporary HOME (and the Tally repo) afterwards
26	```
27	
28	It runs in the background (the dev copy is an accessory app that never takes focus) and needs the dev copies' Claude
29	login (`~/.monocode-hub-dev/claude-config`, Ash's Max account). Budget matters: see "Budget" below.
30	
31	## What it never touches
32	
33	- **Not the daily app.** The copy is a dev slot (`com.ash.monocode-hub.dev.<worktree>-realtest`) under a throwaway
34	  HOME; its identifier is checked against the kind table before anything starts. It never reads
35	  `~/Library/Application Support/com.ash.monocode-hub`, `~/Applications` or `~/.claude`.
36	- **Not Ash's ledger or memory.** Ash OS is the in-process stub (`scripts/hub-stub-server.mjs`) with a throwaway
37	  token. Memory is the run's own invented folder (below), never `~/agent-memory`.
38	- **Not Opus, not max effort.** Every Claude chat goes through `scripts/hub-realtest-claude.mjs`, which holds `--model`
39	  to `sonnet` and `--effort` to `medium` at spawn and on live `set_model` / `apply_flag_settings` (Haiku helper calls,
40	  such as the room's router, stay Haiku and get no effort added, as the app runs them: an added effort made each one
41	  think for 5 to 7 s). The window's own defaults are set to Sonnet 5 + medium as well.
42	- **The temporary HOME's keychain list** is pointed at the login keychain so `claude` can read the dev login (written
43	  to `<tmp HOME>/Library/Preferences/com.apple.security.plist`; the real one is untouched), and
44	  `<tmp HOME>/.monocode-hub-dev/claude-config` is a link to the shared dev config, so the app and Claude agree on where
45	  transcripts live.
46	
47	## How it drives the app
48	
49	`src-tauri/src/verify_live.rs` already lets a dev copy under a temporary HOME read a verify plan. The plan now has a
50	`driver` folder. The run drops one JSON action per file into `<driver>/inbox/`; the window takes them with the
51	`verify_live_take` command, does each, and answers with `verify_live_done` into `<driver>/done/`. Both commands refuse
52	unless this process has a plan with a driver, so the daily app can never use them. The window side is
53	`src/app/model/verifyDriver.ts`, wired in `App.tsx` next to the Stop button's handler. Actions use exactly what Ash's
54	typing and clicks use:
55	
56	| Action | What it calls |
57	| --- | --- |
58	| `send` to a room | GroupChatView's composer path: `sendMessage` / `startConversation` then `simulateReplies` |
59	| `send` to a Mono | `onOpenMono` (the rail click) then the composer's `onSubmit` (queues or steers when busy) |
60	| `send` to a worker | the rail's `openChild` (owner's Mono, then the sub-chat), then `onSubmit` |
61	| `stop` | the Stop button (`delegationTree.stopFromUser`) |
62	| `answer` | Today's Waiting on you row: "Take the pick" (`takePick`) or "answer in your words" + Send (`answerInWords`) |
63	| `open` a hub view | close the Mono view, then `setHubSelection` (Today, Being built, the room); returns the visible text |
64	| `snapshot` | sessions (busy, model, effort, queue, rail state), Monos, rooms with every message, hub localStorage, every `data-hub-*` / `data-mono-*` element |
65	| `drain` | the timestamped log: room messages as they land, typing, every chat's busy/question/queue changes, console errors |
66	| `reload` | `window.location.reload()` once the answer is written: what a vite full reload or View > Reload does to a running turn |
67	| `retry` | the Try again button on a Mono whose last turn failed (rail, Today, Being built: `retryMonoFailure`) |
68	
69	Snapshots carry each chat's last six blocks (`tail`: role, notice, text), and every scenario's evidence keeps what the
70	app answered Claude's own questions with (`answers`, from the `control_response` lines the wrapper logs), so a typed
71	answer is proven to reach the agent, not only the screen.
72	
73	Screenshots: `screencapture -x -o -l <window id>` of the copy's window (found with a tiny Swift CGWindowList script).
74	If capture fails (screen locked, window off-Space) the view's text is still kept and the run says why.
75	
76	## The test project: Tally (`tests/realtest/tally`)
77	
78	A small TypeScript monorepo with zero dependencies to install (Node 22 strips the types): `packages/shared` (types,
79	input checks), `packages/api` (`node:http`: list, create, bump, stats; JSON file store), `packages/ui` (React board
80	and its pure helpers). It is copied fresh into a temporary folder and committed as a new git repo each run.
81	
82	It has what makes delegation, review and stuck cases happen naturally:
83	- **a failing test on purpose** (`median` of an even count), so "fix the tests" is real work with proof;
84	- **a deliberately ambiguous requirement** in the README (the weekly reset and "last week's total");
85	- **a decision only Ash can make** (sharing: public or private), marked "do not build until he picks";
86	- **drift between packages** (the UI's own copy of the tally type) and a backlog (`TODO.md`).
87	
88	The stub lists it as project `tally` with its folder, so the hub makes **Tally lead** and seats the leadership team
89	(Chief of Staff, Projects Manager, frank, Alfred) in `tally:leadership`. The stub's invented Needs are cleared so Today
90	is about this run.
91	
92	## Stand-ins for what the real Ash OS does and the stub doesn't

94	Both are labelled in the evidence, so nobody mistakes them for the service:
95	- **Memory** (`scripts/hub-realtest-memory-mcp.mjs`): a dev copy's chats have no `ash-os` server (harness.rs keeps
96	  only the delegate tool) and the stub has no memory, so the Claude wrapper adds an `ash-os` server with `ash_recall`
97	  (that project plus the global layer, the real rule) and `ash_remember`, over the run's own folder. Seeded from the
98	  scenario file: Tally facts, an EXO fact that must never show up in Tally, and glo…
